Question B-004-001-005.

Why the correct answer is right: A transceiver speech amplifier covers the main voice range used for communications audio: 300 Hz to 3 000 Hz.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "3 Hz to 300 Hz": This range stops where the speech passband is just beginning. It would lose much of the intelligible voice content.
- sourceIndex 2: "300 Hz to 1 000 Hz": This starts at the right lower edge but cuts off the upper speech range needed for clear voice.
- sourceIndex 3: "40 Hz to 40 000 Hz": This is a very wide high-fidelity audio range. It includes sub-voice bass and ultrasonic content, not the narrower communications speech range.
